Home.title: Every rescue animal deserves the right home
Home.lead: Homeward connects rescue organisations with people looking to adopt, with clear information about which animals suit which homes.
Home.adopterBody: Tell us about your home and household, privately. We show you at a glance which animals are a strong match, which might work, and why.
Home.orgBody: Get animals online quickly with structured details, photos and adoption criteria. Your listings live in your own account on the Atmosphere.

GetStarted.title: Get started
GetStarted.intro: Homeward runs on the Atmosphere, the open network behind Bluesky. Your account and your listings belong to you, not to us.
GetStarted.haveAccountHeading: Already on Bluesky or another Atmosphere app?
GetStarted.haveAccountBody: You can use your existing account, wherever it is hosted. Skip to step 2.
GetStarted.step1Heading: 1. Create a free account with Eurosky
GetStarted.step1Body: Eurosky hosts accounts in Europe, under European law. Your handle will look like yourname.eurosky.social. Rescue organisations can later use their own website address as their handle.
GetStarted.step2Body: Sign in to the Bluesky app. If your account is with Eurosky, choose a custom hosting provider and enter {provider}. Then go to Settings → Privacy and security → App passwords, and create one called "Homeward".
GetStarted.step3Body: Use your handle and the app password you just created.
GetStarted.whyBody: An app password lets Homeward publish listings and keep your profile up to date without ever seeing your main password. It can't change your password, email or account settings. You can revoke it at any time in your account settings, and Homeward loses access. Homeward refuses main passwords.

AdopterProfile.title: Your home and preferences
AdopterProfile.intro: Tell us about your home so we can show how well each animal suits you. It takes a few minutes, and you can come back any time.
AdopterProfile.privacyPrivate: Your answers about your household, home and where you live are private. Homeward keeps them encrypted on servers in the EU and uses them only to work out your matches. They're never published, and organisations can't see them unless you choose to share them when you enquire.
AdopterProfile.privacyOptional: Every question is optional. If you'd rather not say, choose “Prefer not to say” and matches show “Not enough information” for that point. We never guess.
AdopterProfile.privacyControl: You can change your answers or delete them at any time.
AdopterProfile.privacyPublic: Separately, you can choose to publish a short public profile to your own account, so organisations can see what you're looking for. It shows only your region and country, never your town or address.

Guidelines.title: Welfare guidelines
Guidelines.intro: How Homeward listings keep animals' welfare first, for the rescues that publish them and the people who adopt.
Guidelines.draft: Draft: these guidelines are being reviewed by rescue and veterinary experts, and they aren't legal advice.

age.heading: Old enough to leave their mother
age.body: Puppies and kittens can be listed from {weeks} weeks old, after time with their mother and litter. Homeward won't publish a listing with a younger puppy or kitten, and says when it can be published. If you only know the year or month of birth, we count the youngest the animal could be.

selling.heading: Rehoming, never selling
selling.body: Homeward is for rescues rehoming animals, not for selling or breeding them. Describe the animal, not a sale: words such as "for sale", "price", "breeder" or "papers" are pointed out before you publish. The adoption fee is shown as no fee, a suggested donation or an adoption fee, never as a price.

honest.heading: Honest descriptions
honest.body: Say what you know about an animal's health, behaviour and needs, and what you don't. Use the criteria to say which homes suit them: adopters see how their own home fits, criterion by criterion.

breeds.heading: Breed rules by country
breeds.body: Some countries ban or restrict certain dog breeds. Homeward warns the rescue when it publishes, and visitors when they view a listing, if a breed may be restricted where the animal or the visitor is.

Report.intro: Tell us if this listing breaks the law or Homeward's rules. A moderator reads every report. {name} isn't told who reported it.

otherIllegal.hint: Something else you believe breaks the law.
